paragraphs: On Saturday morning, Ranger Mark took the Explorers into the small rainforest of the nature park. Teacher Kim walked last, and Lily wrote in her notebook. The air was warm and wet, and the green leaves were very big. The path was wet, the trees were tall, and many insects made a loud noise. "Is anybody tired?" asked Ranger Mark. "No!" said the children. "Today we look for a hornbill," said Ranger Mark.

"Here is a fact," he said. "A hornbill is a big black and white bird with a long yellow beak." "It is possible to see one here, but it is not easy." "How big is it?" asked Mia. "Bigger than a chicken, and it has very big wings," said Ranger Mark. "Where is it?" asked Leo. "We will probably not find it quickly," said Ranger Mark with a smile. "Birds do not come when we shout."

After half an hour, they came to a big fig tree with red fruit. A park worker sat on a small chair under the tree. He held binoculars and a notebook. The notebook had many small marks, one for each bird. He put one finger on his mouth and pointed up at the tree. "He counts birds here every Saturday," whispered Ranger Mark. "From now on, we do not talk."

The children sat down on the ground in a line. May opened her mouth to ask a question, but Lily touched her arm. Mia held her camera in both hands and did not move. Her arms were tired, but she kept the camera ready. For once, Leo did not say a word. Ten minutes passed, and then ten more. A leaf fell from the tree and landed next to May. Nothing else happened, and the forest felt very big.

"Anyway," whispered May, "it was a nice walk." The park worker looked at her and moved his head from side to side. Lily did not look at Mia or May, and she looked only at the tree. Then Lily heard a sound above her. It was deep and slow, like a big fan far away. It was the sound of two large wings. Ranger Mark smiled and did not say a word. Mia lifted her camera, and the top of the fig tree moved. Then, high in the tree, Lily saw a long yellow beak.
text.summary: Ranger Mark takes the Explorers on a walk into the rainforest of the nature park to look for a hornbill. They sit very still and wait, and a park worker helps them.
